claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'd like to check if I'm eligible for Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

To properly assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. I'm a resident here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming you're a UK resident. That's helpful.

To continue assessing Alex's eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about their education or training situation.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training, or has Alex left school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has left school. He's not in college or anything like that at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

I have one more question to clarify Alex's situation:

**Is Alex currently in paid work or self-employment, or is he not working at the moment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has actually started an apprenticeship recently. He's training to be a carpenter.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that - an apprenticeship is important information for eligibility purposes.

I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the relevant rules carefully.

Based on the information you've provided:
- You have one child: Alex, who is 17 years old
- Alex has left school and is not in full-time education
- Alex is currently undertaking an apprenticeship

Under Child Benefit rules, eligibility typically extends to children up to age 16, or in certain circumstances to age 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. However, apprenticeships have specific eligibility criteria that depend on whether they are a recognised apprenticeship and the individual's age and circumstances at the point they started.

**To clarify one final detail: When did Alex start his apprenticeship - was it before or after his 19th birthday?** (Or if he hasn't yet reached 19, this will help me confirm his current age status)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 17, so he started it well before turning 19. He just recently started it, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to make a determination.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Summary:**
- **Child:** Alex (age 17)
- **Eligibility:** ✅ Eligible

**Why:** Alex qualifies for Child Benefit because he is 17 years old and is currently undertaking an apprenticeship, which is recognised as approved training under Child Benefit rules. Child Benefit can be paid for young people up to age 19 if they're in approved training, and Alex meets this criterion.

If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can apply through the official government Child Benefit application process. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
